In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that the output size of a problem is a good indicator for its complexity, even when it is not the sole factor determining the complexity of the problem.
we have improved upon the best known results for a number of fundamental geometric problems, and we have done so by developing a new technique which is of independent interest.
our results are optimal up to poly-logarithmic factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how the known data structures for the problems of ray-shooting and computing linear programming queries can be combined to yield new results for a wide variety of geometric problems.
we show that the output-sensitive lower bounds of Clarkson and Shor [10] for convex hulls, and of Chazelle and Welzl [9] for extreme points, are tight.
we obtain output-sensitive bounds for problems that have been studied in the past, but the previous bounds were only for the case of a constant number of output objects.
